```{python}
#| label: rendered
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import os
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from importlib.metadata import version

import h5py


def run(*argv):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    except OSError:
        return ""


cpu = next(
    (line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for line in open("/proc/cpuinfo") if line.startswith("model name")),
    platform.processor(),
) if os.path.exists("/proc/cpuinfo") else platform.processor()
memory = os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") * os.sysconf("SC_PHYS_PAGES") / 2**30
commit = run("git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD") or "unknown commit"
quarto = run("quarto", "--version") if shutil.which("quarto") else os.environ.get("QUARTO_VERSION", "")
server, repo = os.environ.get("GITHUB_SERVER_URL"), os.environ.get("GITHUB_REPOSITORY")
if server and repo:
    run_url = f"{server}/{repo}/actions/runs/{os.environ.get('GITHUB_RUN_ID')}"
    by = f"by [GitHub Actions]({run_url}) ({os.environ.get('GITHUB_EVENT_NAME')}, `{os.environ.get('GITHUB_REF_NAME')}`)"
    commit = f"[{commit}]({server}/{repo}/commit/{os.environ.get('GITHUB_SHA')})"
else:
    by = f"locally on `{platform.node()}`"
data = os.environ.get("BENCH_DATA_RELEASE")

print(f"""::: {{.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}}
Rendered {datetime.now(timezone.utc):%d %B %Y, %H:%M} UTC {by} ·
**metacooler {version('metacooler')}** at {commit} · **cooler {version('cooler')}** ·
h5py {version('h5py')} (HDF5 {h5py.version.hdf5_version}), numpy {version('numpy')},
pandas {version('pandas')}, pyarrow {version('pyarrow')} · Python {platform.python_version()}{f', Quarto {quarto}' if quarto else ''}  \\
On {cpu}, {os.cpu_count()} cores, {memory:.1f} GB, {platform.system()} {platform.release()} ·
**simulated** datasets {f'from the release [`{data}`]({server}/{repo}/releases/tag/{data})' if data and server else 'generated by simulate.py'}
:::""")
```

Every command below runs **as a fresh process, from bash, as a user would type it**, under GNU `time`
and `timeout`. Each run is one row of `timings.tsv`; every table and figure is drawn from it.
cooler and metacooler get the same inputs and must produce the same contacts — that is checked,
not assumed. cooler is version 0.12.1, the one `uv.lock` pins; `bench.sh` names it, and the
settings cell refuses to time any other.

* **Data.** All four datasets are **simulated**, by
  [`simulate.py`](https://github.com/js2264/metacooler/blob/devel/benchmarks/simulate.py) from a
  fixed seed each. No real reads, assembly or binning is used, so there are no accessions. See
  [Datasets](#datasets) for the model, and what it decides.
* **Replicates.** Every command runs at least 3 times, and up to 5 while its runs add up to
  under 2 min. A command whose single run takes over 10 min runs once (they are listed in
  [Replicates](#replicates)). Tables give the mean ± sd and the number of runs *n*; figures
  draw every run, and the range of its runs as a bar.
* **Measures.** Wall clock; CPU (user + system, children included); peak memory, the largest
  resident set among the command's processes — for cooler's `dump | awk` pipelines, both
  stages' added up, since they run side by side.
* **Cache.** Commands that read a map are timed **warm** (their inputs in the page cache, read
  just before) and **cold** (their inputs evicted from it before every run, so they come from
  the disk). Commands that write a map are timed warm.
* **Time limit.** A run still going after the time limit (30 min) is stopped by `timeout`. Its
  time and memory are where it was stopped: measured lower bounds, never extrapolations. A run
  the kernel kills for want of memory is reported as out of memory.

```bash
# Render (runs the benchmarks: hours for the full ladder; minutes for S and M)
uv sync && source .venv/bin/activate
cd benchmarks && quarto render benchmarks.qmd
BENCH_DATASETS="S M" quarto render benchmarks.qmd   # a quick look
```

`bench.sh` holds the settings and the one timing function, `bench`; `simulate.py` makes the
datasets; `targets.py` picks what the queries ask for; `pagecache.py` evicts the inputs of a cold
run. A second render re-uses runs already in `timings.tsv` (`BENCH_REDO=1` times them again). The
[Benchmarks workflow](https://github.com/js2264/metacooler/blob/devel/.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml)
renders this page for every release, and on demand, and publishes it with the
[metacooler documentation](https://js2264.github.io/metacooler/).

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Setup: paths, colours, table and figure helpers"
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter, LogLocator, NullLocator

WORK = Path(os.environ.get("BENCH_WORK", "_work")).resolve()
RESULTS = Path(os.environ.get("BENCH_RESULTS", "_results")).resolve()
DATA, MAPS, QUERIES = WORK / "data", WORK / "maps", WORK / "queries"
FIGURES = RESULTS / "figures"
FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
DATASETS = os.environ.get("BENCH_DATASETS", "S M L XL").split()
TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("BENCH_TIMEOUT", 1800))
LONG = float(os.environ.get("BENCH_LONG", 600))

# Colour is identity: a tool keeps its hue in every figure (validated for
# colour-blind separation); the datasets, ordered by size, one hue light to dark.
HUE = {"metacooler": "#2a78d6", "cooler": "#eb6834"}
SIZE = dict(zip(["S", "M", "L", "XL"], ["#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b"]))
INK, INK2, GRID, SURFACE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e7e6e2", "#fcfcfb"
COLD = (0, (4, 2))  # cold runs: dashed lines, open markers
plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.facecolor": SURFACE, "savefig.facecolor": SURFACE,
    "axes.edgecolor": INK2, "axes.labelcolor": INK, "xtick.color": INK2, "ytick.color": INK2,
    "text.color": INK, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID, "grid.linewidth": 0.6, "axes.axisbelow": True,
    "lines.linewidth": 2, "font.size": 9, "axes.titlesize": 10, "axes.titleweight": "bold",
    "axes.titlelocation": "left", "legend.frameon": False,
})


def save(fig, name):
    """Show a figure; keep it as PNG and SVG beside the tables."""
    fig.savefig(FIGURES / f"{name}.png", dpi=200)
    fig.savefig(FIGURES / f"{name}.svg")
    plt.show()


def show(frame, **formats):
    """A table without row numbers."""
    return frame.style.hide(axis="index").format(formats or None, na_rep="")


def timings():
    """Every run, one row each, with the size of its dataset."""
    t = pd.read_csv(RESULTS / "timings.tsv", sep="\t")
    t = t[t["dataset"].isin(DATASETS)].copy()
    t["contigs"] = t["dataset"].map(CONTIGS)
    t["peak_gb"] = t["peak_mb"] / 1024
    return t


def runs(t, **match):
    """The rows of t whose columns equal the values given."""
    keep = np.ones(len(t), bool)
    for column, value in match.items():
        keep &= (t[column] == value).to_numpy()
    return t[keep]


def finished(section, dataset, tool, task):
    """Whether a command's last run, warm or cold, finished: its output is there to check."""
    r = runs(timings(), section=section, dataset=dataset, tool=tool, task=task)
    r = r[r["status"] != "skipped"]
    return len(r) > 0 and r["status"].iloc[-1] == "ok"


def ram(t):
    """The memory of the machine the runs were on (GB)."""
    known = pd.to_numeric(t["memory_gb"], errors="coerce").dropna()
    return float(known.iloc[0]) if len(known) else float("nan")


def digits_for(x):
    """As many decimals as a number's size needs: 0.452, 4.52, 45.2, 452."""
    x = abs(x)
    return 3 if x < 1 else 2 if x < 10 else 1 if x < 100 else 0


def human(s):
    """Seconds as ms, s or min: 650 ms, 61.3 s, 30 min."""
    if s is None or s != s:
        return "–"
    value, unit = (s * 1e3, "ms") if s < 1 else (s, "s") if s < 120 else (s / 60, "min")
    return f"{value:,.0f} ms" if unit == "ms" else f"{value:,.1f}".removesuffix(".0") + f" {unit}"


def cell(rows, value="wall_s", digits=None, spread=True):
    """Mean ± sd (n) over the runs that finished; else what became of the command."""
    ok = rows.loc[rows["status"] == "ok", value]
    if len(ok):
        d = digits_for(ok.mean()) if digits is None else digits
        text = f"{ok.mean():,.{d}f}"
        if spread:
            text += (f" ± {ok.std():,.{d}f}" if len(ok) > 1 else "") + f" (n={len(ok)})"
        return text
    if not len(rows):
        return ""
    last = rows.iloc[-1]
    if last["status"] == "timeout":
        if value == "wall_s":
            return f"> {last['wall_s']:,.0f} (stopped at the time limit)"
        if value == "peak_mb":
            return f"≥ {last[value]:,.0f} (when stopped)" if last[value] == last[value] else "not measured (stopped)"
        return "–"
    if last["status"] == "oom":
        if value == "wall_s":
            return f"out of memory after {last[value]:,.0f} s"
        return f"out of memory at {last[value]:,.0f}" if value == "peak_mb" else "–"
    return {"skipped": "not run", "error": "FAILED"}.get(last["status"], last["status"])


def wide(section, value="wall_s", digits=None, spread=True, cache="warm"):
    """One row per command, one column per dataset."""
    t = runs(timings(), section=section, cache=cache)
    keys = ["tool", "task", "dataset"]
    cells = pd.DataFrame(
        [(*k, cell(g, value, digits, spread)) for k, g in t.groupby(keys, sort=False)],
        columns=[*keys, "cell"],
    )
    out = cells.pivot(index=["tool", "task"], columns="dataset", values="cell")
    out = out.reindex(list(dict.fromkeys(zip(cells["tool"], cells["task"]))))
    return out.reindex(columns=[d for d in DATASETS if d in out.columns]).reset_index()


def compact(n):
    """1,000 as 1k, 2,000,000 as 2M: tick labels that fit three panels abreast."""
    for div, unit in ((1e6, "M"), (1e3, "k")):
        if n >= div:
            return f"{n / div:.3g}{unit}"
    return f"{n:,}"


def contig_axis(ax):
    """Datasets along x, at their contig counts."""
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.xaxis.set_minor_locator(NullLocator())
    ax.set_xticks(
        [CONTIGS[d] for d in DATASETS],
        [f"{d}\n{compact(CONTIGS[d])}" for d in DATASETS],
    )
    ax.set_xlim(min(CONTIGS.values()) / 2.5, max(CONTIGS.values()) * 2.5)
    ax.set_xlabel("contigs in the assembly")


def log_y(ax, label):
    """A log axis labelled at 1, 2, 5 of each decade, so that a short range still reads."""
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:g}"))
    ax.yaxis.set_minor_locator(NullLocator())
    ax.set_ylabel(label)


def seconds_axis(ax, unit="s"):
    log_y(ax, f"wall clock ({unit})")


def stopped(ax, x, y, colour, status):
    """A run that did not finish, where it ended. Stopped at the time limit: a
    bar with an arrow up, since it would have taken longer -- a lower bound,
    measured where timeout killed it. Killed for want of memory: a cross."""
    if status == "timeout":
        ax.scatter([x], [y], marker="_", s=160, color=colour, lw=2.5, zorder=5)
        ax.annotate("", xy=(x, y * 2.4), xytext=(x, y), zorder=5,
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=colour, lw=1.5, mutation_scale=10))
        ax.annotate("stopped at\nthe time limit", (x, y * 1.55), xytext=(-7, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                    ha="right", va="center", color=INK2, fontsize=7.5, zorder=6,
                    bbox=dict(boxstyle="square,pad=0.1", fc=SURFACE, ec="none"))
        ax.update_datalim([(x, y * 2.8)])
    else:
        ax.scatter([x], [y], marker="X", s=60, color=colour, zorder=5)
        ax.annotate("out of memory", (x, y), xytext=(0, 9), textcoords="offset points",
                    ha="center", color=INK2, fontsize=7.5)


def scaling(ax, rows, value="wall_s"):
    """One line per command and cache state through the means of its runs;
    every run a dot, and a bar from its fastest to its slowest. Cold: dashed,
    open markers. A run that did not finish is drawn where it ended (see
    `stopped`), and no line joins it: nothing is extrapolated."""
    for (tool, _task, cache), r in rows.groupby(["tool", "task", "cache"], sort=False):
        colour, cold = HUE[tool], cache == "cold"
        ok = r[r["status"] == "ok"]
        stats = ok.groupby("contigs")[value].agg(["mean", "min", "max"])
        if len(stats):
            ax.errorbar(stats.index, stats["mean"],
                        yerr=[stats["mean"] - stats["min"], stats["max"] - stats["mean"]],
                        color=colour, ls=COLD if cold else "-", lw=1.6 if cold else 2,
                        marker="o", ms=5, mfc=SURFACE if cold else colour, mec=colour,
                        capsize=2.5, elinewidth=1, zorder=3)
            ax.scatter(ok["contigs"], ok[value], s=9, color=colour, alpha=0.35, lw=0, zorder=4)
        for _, run in r[r["status"].isin(["timeout", "oom"]) & r[value].notna()].iterrows():
            stopped(ax, run["contigs"], run[value], colour, run["status"])
        for x in r.loc[r["status"] == "skipped", "contigs"]:
            ax.annotate(f"{tool}\nnot run", (x, 0.03), xycoords=("data", "axes fraction"),
                        ha="center", va="bottom", color=colour, fontsize=7.5)
    contig_axis(ax)


def limit_line(ax, rows):
    """The time limit, where a run in the panel reached it."""
    if (rows["status"] == "timeout").any():
        ax.axhline(TIMEOUT, color=INK2, lw=0.8, ls=(0, (1, 2)), zorder=1)
        ax.annotate(f"time limit, {human(TIMEOUT)}", (0.02, TIMEOUT), xycoords=("axes fraction", "data"),
                    xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", color=INK2, fontsize=7.5)


def ram_line(ax, gb, vertical=False):
    """The memory of the machine the runs were on."""
    if gb != gb:
        return
    if vertical:
        ax.axvline(gb, color=INK2, lw=1, ls=(0, (4, 2)), zorder=1)
        ax.annotate(f"RAM of this machine\n{gb:.1f} GB", (gb, 1.0), xycoords=("data", "axes fraction"),
                    xytext=(-4, -2), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", va="top",
                    color=INK2, fontsize=7.5)
    else:
        ax.axhline(gb, color=INK2, lw=1, ls=(0, (4, 2)), zorder=1)
        ax.annotate(f"RAM of this machine, {gb:.1f} GB", (0.02, gb), xycoords=("axes fraction", "data"),
                    xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", color=INK2, fontsize=7.5)
        ax.update_datalim([(min(CONTIGS.values()), gb * 1.6)])


COMMANDS = {
    ("create", "cload pairs"): "cooler cload pairs",
    ("create", "create pairs"): "metacooler create pairs",
    ("convert", "create cool"): "metacooler create cool",
    ("convert", "flatten"): "metacooler flatten",
    ("query", "contig", "cooler"): "cooler dump -r (a contig)",
    ("query", "contig", "metacooler"): "metacooler dump -r (a contig)",
    ("query", "genome", "cooler"): "cooler dump --join | awk (a genome)",
    ("query", "genome", "metacooler"): "metacooler dump -r (a genome)",
    ("query", "genome pair", "cooler"): "cooler dump --join | awk (a genome pair)",
    ("query", "genome pair", "metacooler"): "metacooler dump -r -r2 (a genome pair)",
    ("aggregate", "genome network", "cooler"): "cooler dump --join | awk (genome network)",
    ("aggregate", "genome network", "metacooler"): "metacooler network --level genome",
    ("aggregate", "genome-level .cool"): "metacooler aggregate --level genome",
}


def command(section, tool, task):
    """What a user types, in a few words: the name a sentence gives a command."""
    return COMMANDS.get((section, task, tool)) or COMMANDS.get((section, task)) or f"{tool} {task}"


TOOLS_LEGEND = [Line2D([], [], color=HUE[t], marker="o", ms=5, label=t) for t in ("cooler", "metacooler")]
CACHE_LEGEND = [
    Line2D([], [], color=INK2, marker="o", ms=5, label="warm"),
    Line2D([], [], color=INK2, ls=COLD, lw=1.6, marker="o", ms=5, mfc=SURFACE, label="cold (inputs evicted)"),
]
```

## Settings

```{python}
#| label: settings
%%bash
source bench.sh
echo "datasets: $DATASETS · bin size: $BINSIZE bp · zoom levels: $ZOOMS"
echo "time limit: $TIMEOUT s per run"
if [[ -n ${BENCH_REPS:-} ]]; then
    echo "runs per command: $BENCH_REPS"
else
    echo "runs per command: $MIN_REPS to $MAX_REPS (no more than $MIN_REPS once they add up to $BUDGET s;"
    echo "  one, for a command whose run takes over $LONG s)"
fi
metacooler --version
cooler --version
# Every timing is against one cooler: refuse to time another.
installed=$(python -c 'import cooler; print(cooler.__version__)')
if [[ $installed != "$COOLER_VERSION" ]]; then
    echo "cooler $installed is installed; these benchmarks are against cooler $COOLER_VERSION." >&2
    echo "Run uv sync (uv.lock pins it), or bump COOLER_VERSION in bench.sh with the lock." >&2
    exit 1
fi
# Cold runs evict their inputs from the page cache: check this file system lets them.
probe=$WORK/.evict-probe
head -c 8388608 /dev/urandom >"$probe" && warm "$probe"
if python pagecache.py evict "$probe"; then
    echo "cold runs: inputs evicted from the page cache before every run ($(python pagecache.py resident "$probe" | cut -f1) left cached in a test)"
else
    echo "cold runs: this file system keeps its files in memory; cold runs will be skipped" >&2
fi
rm -f "$probe"
```

## Datasets

**All four datasets are simulated.** No real reads, assembly or binning enters them, so they have
no accessions. Each is drawn by
[`simulate.py`](https://github.com/js2264/metacooler/blob/devel/benchmarks/simulate.py) from a
preset and a fixed seed, so every render times the same data; the workflow publishes them as a
release (`benchmark-data-v<generator version>`) and fetches them from there.

* **Genomes.** MAGs (log-normal, 2.5 Mb median) and small bins standing for plasmids, phages and
  other mobile elements (20 kb median) are binned. Low-abundance genomes that no binner would
  recover make up the rest of the assembly, and their contigs end up in `__unbinned__`.
* **Contigs.** Each genome is cut around its own median contig length, so one MAG comes out in a
  dozen long contigs and the next in hundreds of short ones. Unbinned contigs are short (~0.9 kb).
  Nothing is under 500 bp. The assembly lists contigs in random order, as an assembler does,
  so a genome's contigs are scattered through any genome-agnostic `.cool`.
* **Contacts.** A pair falls in a genome in proportion to abundance × length; 96 % stay there, at a
  P(s) ~ 1/s separation (60 %) or uniformly along a circular chromosome (40 %); 4 % join two
  genomes. Which pairs are intra-contig, inter-contig or inter-genome then follows from the
  contig lengths, as in a real library.

The presets are sized after real metagenomic Hi-C maps — M about a mock community's, L about a
human gut sample's, in genomes, contigs, bins and contacts — but no data of those maps is used.
What the simulation decides matters most for the genome queries (§5): cooler scans every pixel of
the map, metacooler reads those of one genome, so their ratio follows the share of the map's
pixels the queried genome holds. That share is set here by the model's community — how many
genomes, how abundant — not by a sample; the query table gives it for each dataset.

```{python}
#| label: datasets-make
%%bash
source bench.sh
for ds in $DATASETS; do  # fetched, made earlier, or made now
    python simulate.py --preset "$ds" --outdir "$DATA/$ds" --keep | sed "s|$WORK/||"
done
cd "$WORK" && du -sh data/*
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-datasets
#| tbl-cap: "The four simulated datasets. Contig N50 is that of the whole assembly; MAG contig N50 is the median over MAGs of each MAG's own contig N50. Pair categories are the generated truth, measured against the binning."
#| code-fold: true
SUMMARY = {ds: json.loads((DATA / ds / "summary.json").read_text()) for ds in DATASETS}
CONTIGS = {ds: s["contigs"] for ds, s in SUMMARY.items()}
BINSIZE = int(os.environ.get("BENCH_BINSIZE", 1000))
SIZES = {
    ds: pd.read_csv(DATA / ds / "contigs.sizes", sep="\t", header=None, names=["contig", "length"])
    for ds in DATASETS
}
rows = []
for ds, s in SUMMARY.items():
    rows.append({
        "dataset": ds,
        "source": f"simulated (simulate.py v{s['generator_version']}, seed {s['seed']})",
        "genomes (MAGs + small bins)": f"{s['genomes']:,} ({s['mags']:,} + {s['mge_bins']:,})",
        "contigs": f"{s['contigs']:,}",
        "binned contigs": f"{s['binned_contigs'] / s['contigs']:.0%}",
        "assembly (Mb)": f"{s['assembly_bp'] / 1e6:,.0f}",
        "contig N50 (kb)": f"{s['contig_n50'] / 1e3:.1f}",
        "median contig (bp)": f"{s['contig_median']:,}",
        "contigs / MAG (median)": f"{s['contigs_per_mag_median']:,.0f}",
        "MAG size (median, Mb)": f"{s['mag_bp_median'] / 1e6:.2f}",
        "MAG contig N50 (kb)": f"{s['mag_contig_n50_median'] / 1e3:.1f}",
        "read pairs (M)": f"{s['pairs'] / 1e6:,.0f}",
        "intra-contig": f"{s['pairs_intra_contig']:.1%}",
        "inter-contig, intra-genome": f"{s['pairs_inter_contig_intra_genome']:.1%}",
        "inter-genome": f"{s['pairs_inter_genome']:.1%}",
        "unbinned, inter-contig": f"{s['pairs_unbinned']:.1%}",
        f"bins at {BINSIZE:,} bp": f"{int((-(-SIZES[ds]['length'] // BINSIZE)).sum()):,}",
        "pairs.gz (MB)": f"{s['files_bytes']['contacts.pairs.gz'] / 1e6:,.0f}",
        "pairs md5 (uncompressed)": s["pairs_md5_uncompressed"][:12],
    })
DATASET_TABLE = pd.DataFrame(rows)
DATASET_TABLE.to_csv(RESULTS / "datasets.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
show(DATASET_TABLE.set_index("dataset").T.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": ""}))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-datasets
#| fig-cap: "What the simulated datasets are made of: contig lengths, as the share of contigs in log-spaced bins (left), and how many contigs a binned genome has, as the share of genomes with at least that many (right)."
#| code-fold: true
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.2), layout="constrained")
for ds in DATASETS:
    sizes = SIZES[ds]
    binning = pd.read_csv(DATA / ds / "contigs.tsv", sep="\t", usecols=[0, 1])
    per_genome = binning.loc[binning["genome_name"] != "__unbinned__", "genome_name"].value_counts()
    edges = np.geomspace(500, sizes["length"].max() + 1, 30)
    share, _ = np.histogram(sizes["length"], edges)
    left.plot(np.sqrt(edges[1:] * edges[:-1]), share / share.sum(), color=SIZE[ds], label=ds)
    n = np.sort(per_genome.to_numpy())
    right.step(n, 1 - np.arange(len(n)) / len(n), where="post", color=SIZE[ds], label=ds)
for ax, xlabel, ylabel in ((left, "contig length (bp)", "share of contigs"),
                           (right, "contigs per binned genome", "share of genomes with at least as many")):
    ax.set(xscale="log", xlabel=xlabel, ylabel=ylabel)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.0%}"))
left.legend(title="dataset")
save(fig, "datasets")
```

## 1 · Creating a map from pairs

`cooler cload pairs` and `metacooler create pairs`, on the same pairs, contig lengths and bin size;
metacooler also reads the binning and genome tables and builds `/genomes`, its index, the QC
block and the per-MAG P(s) table — its defaults, all on.

On a metagenome the difference is the contig count, not the pixels. `cooler.create` types
`/bins/chrom` as an HDF5 enumeration with one member per contig. Building it is quadratic,
because each insertion rescans the members already there, and past a few thousand contigs the
type outgrows HDF5's object header anyway and is dropped for plain integers. `cooler cload pairs`
sorts externally: it writes the bin table once per chunk of pairs and once per merge, so it pays
that cost several times per file. metacooler writes the integers directly.

```{python}
#| label: create
%%bash
source bench.sh
for ds in $DATASETS; do
    d=$DATA/$ds
    warm "$d/contacts.pairs.gz"
    bench create "$ds" cooler "cload pairs" "$MAPS/$ds.cool" -- \
        cooler cload pairs -c1 2 -p1 3 -c2 4 -p2 5 \
            "$d/contigs.sizes:$BINSIZE" "$d/contacts.pairs.gz" "$MAPS/$ds.cool"
    bench create "$ds" metacooler "create pairs" "$MAPS/$ds.metacool" -- \
        metacooler create pairs --pairs "$d/contacts.pairs.gz" --bins "$BINSIZE" \
            --contigs "$d/contigs.tsv" --genomes "$d/genomes.tsv" -o "$MAPS/$ds.metacool"
done
```

A run stopped by timeout at the time limit (dotted) is a bar with an arrow up, where it was stopped: a measured lower bound, which no line joins and nothing extrapolates. Right, dashed: the RAM of the machine."

The two tools must hold the same contacts: same number of pixels, same total, read from each
file's own attributes.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-same-contacts
#| tbl-cap: "The contacts each tool's map holds: pixels (nnz) and their total, from the file's own attributes."
#| code-fold: true
MADE_BY = {"cooler": ("cload pairs", "cool"), "metacooler": ("create pairs", "metacool")}
same = []
for ds in DATASETS:
    row, held = {"dataset": ds}, {}
    for tool, (task, ext) in MADE_BY.items():
        if finished("create", ds, tool, task):  # else the map below is not this tool's
            with h5py.File(MAPS / f"{ds}.{ext}", "r") as f:
                held[tool] = int(f.attrs["nnz"]), int(f.attrs["sum"])
            row[f"{tool} nnz"], row[f"{tool} sum"] = held[tool]
    missing = [tool for tool in MADE_BY if tool not in held]
    row["identical"] = (
        f"{' and '.join(missing)} did not finish" if missing
        else "yes" if held["cooler"] == held["metacooler"] else "NO"
    )
    same.append(row)
same = pd.DataFrame(same)
assert not (same["identical"] == "NO").any(), "cooler and metacooler disagree on the contacts"
show(same, **{c: "{:,.0f}" for c in same.columns if c.endswith(("nnz", "sum"))})
```

Where cooler did not finish, the rest of the page still needs the genome-agnostic `.cool`. It
is built here, untimed, by metacooler in the assembly's own contig order (`--contig-order fasta`,
which reproduces `cooler cload pairs` pixel for pixel), then flattened to a plain cooler.

```{python}
#| label: cool-fallback
%%bash
source bench.sh
for ds in $DATASETS; do
    [[ -s $MAPS/$ds.cool ]] && continue
    d=$DATA/$ds
    echo "$ds: no $ds.cool from cooler; building it with metacooler"
    metacooler create pairs -q --contig-order fasta --no-qc --no-ps --pairs "$d/contacts.pairs.gz" \
        --bins "$BINSIZE" --contigs "$d/contigs.tsv" -o "$SCRATCH/$ds.fasta.metacool" &&
        metacooler flatten -q "$SCRATCH/$ds.fasta.metacool" -o "$MAPS/$ds.cool"
    rm -f "$SCRATCH/$ds.fasta.metacool" "$SCRATCH/$ds.fasta.ps.tsv"
done
cd "$MAPS" && du -h -- *.cool *.metacool
```

## 2 · Size on disk

What it takes to keep a metagenome's map with its genomes, on disk, four ways:

* **`.metacool`**: one file, every contig and contact, with the binning, the genome and contig
  tables, their index and the QC block (`metacooler create pairs`, above).
* **`.cool` + binning tables**: the genome-agnostic `.cool` (`cooler cload pairs`) and, beside it,
  the tables that say which contig is in which genome and what each genome is — here
  `simulate.py`'s `contigs.tsv` (contig, genome, GC, coverage) and `genomes.tsv` (completeness,
  contamination, quality, GC, abundance), the kind of tables a binner such as MetaTOR writes. The
  `.cool` alone holds the same contacts, without knowing a genome from another.
* **One `.cool` per MAG**: each MAG's contigs and the contacts within it, one file per MAG — the
  MAGs only, the way they are usually handed on. They hold less than the others: no unbinned
  contig, no small bin, no contact between two genomes. The table below says how much less.
  Written untimed by `metacooler extract --split`, through cooler's own writer, so they are the
  files cooler itself writes for those contigs and contacts.

The input pairs (`contacts.pairs.gz`) are given for scale.

```{python}
#| label: storage-make
%%bash
source bench.sh
# simulate.py names the MAGs MAG_*: the filter picks them out of /genomes.
for ds in $DATASETS; do
    out=$MAPS/$ds.mags
    [[ -e $out/.complete && $out/.complete -nt $MAPS/$ds.metacool ]] && continue
    rm -rf "$out" && mkdir -p "$out"
    metacooler extract -q "$MAPS/$ds.metacool" --filter 'genomes.name =~ ^MAG_' --split -o "$out/$ds" &&
        touch "$out/.complete"
done
cd "$MAPS" && du -sh -- *.mags
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-storage
#| tbl-cap: "Size on disk (MB) of each way to keep the map with its genomes, and how many files it takes. The `.cool` is cooler's own where cooler finished, and the untimed one built above where it did not."
#| code-fold: true
def held_by(path):
    """Contigs, pixels and contacts a cool or metacool holds, from its own attributes."""
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as f:
        return len(f["chroms/name"]), int(f.attrs["nnz"]), int(f.attrs["sum"])


STORAGE, HELD, MAG_SHARE = [], [], {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    d = DATA / ds
    tables = (d / "contigs.tsv").stat().st_size + (d / "genomes.tsv").stat().st_size
    cool = (MAPS / f"{ds}.cool").stat().st_size
    mags = sorted((MAPS / f"{ds}.mags").glob("*.cool"))
    for option, files, size in (
        (".metacool", 1, (MAPS / f"{ds}.metacool").stat().st_size),
        (".cool + binning tables", 3, cool + tables),
        (".cool alone (no genomes)", 1, cool),
        ("one .cool per MAG", len(mags), sum(p.stat().st_size for p in mags)),
        ("contacts.pairs.gz (input)", 1, (d / "contacts.pairs.gz").stat().st_size),
    ):
        STORAGE.append({"dataset": ds, "contigs": CONTIGS[ds], "option": option, "files": files, "mb": size / 1e6})
    contigs, nnz, total = held_by(MAPS / f"{ds}.metacool")
    in_mags = np.array([held_by(p) for p in mags]).reshape(-1, 3).sum(axis=0)
    MAG_SHARE[ds] = {"contigs": in_mags[0] / contigs, "pixels": in_mags[1] / nnz, "contacts": in_mags[2] / total}
    HELD.append({
        "dataset": ds, "MAG files": f"{len(mags):,}",
        "contigs": f"{in_mags[0]:,} of {contigs:,} ({in_mags[0] / contigs:.1%})",
        "pixels": f"{in_mags[1]:,} of {nnz:,} ({in_mags[1] / nnz:.1%})",
        "contacts": f"{in_mags[2]:,} of {total:,} ({in_mags[2] / total:.1%})",
    })
STORAGE = pd.DataFrame(STORAGE)
STORAGE.to_csv(RESULTS / "storage.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
OPTIONS = list(dict.fromkeys(STORAGE["option"]))
table = STORAGE.assign(
    cell=[f"{mb:,.1f}" + (f" ({files:,} files)" if files > 1 else "") for mb, files in zip(STORAGE["mb"], STORAGE["files"])]
).pivot(index="option", columns="dataset", values="cell").reindex(index=OPTIONS, columns=DATASETS)
show(table.rename_axis("MB on disk").reset_index())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-mag-files
#| tbl-cap: "What the per-MAG `.cool` files hold, out of the whole map (the .metacool and the .cool hold all of it)."
#| code-fold: true
show(pd.DataFrame(HELD))
```

## 4 · Multi-resolution maps

`cooler zoomify` and `metacooler zoomify`, to the same resolutions. Each coarser level is another
`cooler.create`, so cooler pays the per-contig cost once per level. Where cooler could not build
the base map, its pyramid is not attempted.

```{python}
#| label: zoomify
%%bash
source bench.sh
for ds in $DATASETS; do
    warm "$MAPS/$ds.cool" "$MAPS/$ds.metacool"
    bench zoomify "$ds" metacooler zoomify "$SCRATCH/$ds.mmetacool" -- \
        metacooler zoomify "$MAPS/$ds.metacool" -r "$ZOOMS" -o "$SCRATCH/$ds.mmetacool"
    if unfinished create "$ds" cooler "cload pairs"; then
        skip zoomify "$ds" cooler zoomify "cooler cload pairs did not finish on $ds"
        continue
    fi
    bench zoomify "$ds" cooler zoomify "$SCRATCH/$ds.mcool" -- \
        cooler zoomify -r "$ZOOMS" -o "$SCRATCH/$ds.mcool" "$MAPS/$ds.cool"
done
```

## 5 · Querying a contig, a genome, a genome pair

One contig, one MAG and one pair of MAGs per dataset, picked by `targets.py` with a fixed seed
(the pair in proportion to abundance × length, as the library joins genomes, so that it shares
contacts). cooler serves a contig through its own index (`dump -r`). It has no notion of a genome. So a MAG's
pixels are the joined pixels whose two contigs the binning table puts in that MAG, in one pass of
`awk` over the whole map. metacooler resolves the genome by name (`dump -r`/`-r2`).

Each query is timed twice. **Warm**: its inputs (the map, and for cooler's scans the binning
table) are read just before, so they are in the page cache, as on a machine that has just written
or read the map. **Cold**: they are evicted from the page cache before every run, so their bytes
come from the disk (`pagecache.py`: `posix_fadvise`, then a check with `mincore` that they are
gone). In both, Python and the libraries are already cached, as on any machine that ran them
recently: a first run after a boot also pays for loading those, the same for both tools. On a
cloud machine the disk may be cached by its host too: cold, here, means not in this machine's
memory.

```{python}
#| label: query-cli
%%bash
source bench.sh
in_genome='NR == FNR { if ($2 == g) keep[$1]; next } ($1 in keep) && ($4 in keep)'
in_pair='NR == FNR { if ($2 == a) A[$1]; if ($2 == b) B[$1]; next }'
in_pair+=' (($1 in A) && ($4 in B)) || (($1 in B) && ($4 in A))'
for ds in $DATASETS; do
    d=$DATA/$ds m=$MAPS/$ds q=$QUERIES/$ds
    read -r contig mag a b <<<"$(python targets.py --contigs "$d/contigs.tsv" \
        --sizes "$d/contigs.sizes" --genomes "$d/genomes.tsv")"
    echo "$ds: contig $contig · genome $mag · genome pair $a × $b"
    # Each twice: warm, then cold (the files named first evicted before every run).
    both "$m.cool" query "$ds" cooler contig "$q.cooler.contig.tsv" -- \
        cooler dump -t pixels -r "$contig" -o "$q.cooler.contig.tsv" "$m.cool"
    both "$m.metacool" query "$ds" metacooler contig "$q.metacooler.contig.tsv" -- \
        metacooler dump "$m.metacool" -t pixels -r "$contig" -o "$q.metacooler.contig.tsv"
    both "$m.cool $d/contigs.tsv" query "$ds" cooler genome "$q.cooler.genome.tsv" -- bash -o pipefail -c \
        "$STAGE cooler dump -t pixels --join $m.cool | $STAGE awk -F'\t' -v g=$mag '$in_genome' $d/contigs.tsv - > $q.cooler.genome.tsv"
    both "$m.metacool" query "$ds" metacooler genome "$q.metacooler.genome.tsv" -- \
        metacooler dump "$m.metacool" -t pixels -r "$mag" -o "$q.metacooler.genome.tsv"
    both "$m.cool $d/contigs.tsv" query "$ds" cooler "genome pair" "$q.cooler.pair.tsv" -- bash -o pipefail -c \
        "$STAGE cooler dump -t pixels --join $m.cool | $STAGE awk -F'\t' -v a=$a -v b=$b '$in_pair' $d/contigs.tsv - > $q.cooler.pair.tsv"
    both "$m.metacool" query "$ds" metacooler "genome pair" "$q.metacooler.pair.tsv" -- \
        metacooler dump "$m.metacool" -t pixels -r "$a" -r2 "$b" -o "$q.metacooler.pair.tsv"
done
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-query-cli
#| tbl-cap: "Queries from the command line, warm: wall-clock seconds, mean ± sd (n runs)."
#| code-fold: true
def pixels(path):
    """Rows and contact total of a dump: the count is the last column."""
    if not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size == 0:
        return 0, 0
    last = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", header=None).iloc[:, -1]
    return len(last), int(last.sum())


SHARE = {}  # the share of the map's pixels each query returned: what the scan's cost is set against
agree = []
for ds in DATASETS:
    with h5py.File(MAPS / f"{ds}.metacool", "r") as f:
        nnz = int(f.attrs["nnz"])
    for name, file in (("contig", "contig"), ("genome", "genome"), ("genome pair", "pair")):
        got = {tool: pixels(QUERIES / f"{ds}.{tool}.{file}.tsv")
               for tool in ("metacooler", "cooler") if finished("query", ds, tool, name)}
        missing = [tool for tool in ("cooler", "metacooler") if tool not in got]
        n, total = next(iter(got.values()), (None, None))
        if n is not None:
            SHARE[ds, name] = n / nnz
        agree.append({
            "dataset": ds, "query": name,
            "pixels": "–" if n is None else f"{n:,}",
            "share of the map's pixels": "–" if n is None else f"{n / nnz:.3%}",
            "contacts": "–" if total is None else f"{total:,}",
            "same as cooler": f"{' and '.join(missing)} did not finish" if missing
                              else "yes" if got["cooler"] == got["metacooler"] else "NO",
        })
agree = pd.DataFrame(agree)
assert not (agree["same as cooler"] == "NO").any(), "the two tools returned different pixels"
show(wide("query"))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-query-cold
#| tbl-cap: "Queries from the command line, cold (inputs evicted from the page cache before every run): wall-clock seconds, mean ± sd (n runs)."
#| code-fold: true
show(wide("query", cache="cold"))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-query-pixels
#| tbl-cap: "What each query returned (the two tools must agree), and the share of the map's pixels that is: cooler's scans read every pixel of the map, metacooler's reads only these."
#| code-fold: true
show(agree)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-query-memory
#| tbl-cap: "Queries: peak memory (MB), warm, mean ± sd (n runs); for cooler's dump | awk pipelines, both stages added up."
#| code-fold: true
show(wide("query", "peak_mb", digits=0))
```

## 6 · Genome-level aggregation

The genome × genome contact network: `metacooler network --level genome`, against the same
edge list from cooler (`dump --join`, then an `awk` sum over the binning table), both warm and
cold, as the queries above. And the aggregated genome-level `.cool` (`metacooler aggregate --level
genome`), which cooler has no command for.

```{python}
#| label: aggregate
%%bash
source bench.sh
by_genome='NR == FNR { g[$1] = $2; next }'
by_genome+=' { a = g[$1]; b = g[$4]; if (a > b) { t = a; a = b; b = t }; n[a "\t" b] += $7 }'
by_genome+=' END { for (k in n) print k "\t" n[k] }'
for ds in $DATASETS; do
    d=$DATA/$ds m=$MAPS/$ds q=$QUERIES/$ds
    both "$m.cool $d/contigs.tsv" aggregate "$ds" cooler "genome network" "$q.cooler.network.tsv" -- bash -o pipefail -c \
        "$STAGE cooler dump -t pixels --join $m.cool | $STAGE awk -F'\t' '$by_genome' $d/contigs.tsv - > $q.cooler.network.tsv"
    both "$m.metacool" aggregate "$ds" metacooler "genome network" "$q.metacooler.network.tsv" -- \
        metacooler network "$m.metacool" --level genome -o "$q.metacooler.network.tsv"
    warm "$m.metacool"
    bench aggregate "$ds" metacooler "genome-level .cool" "$SCRATCH/$ds.genomes.cool" -- \
        metacooler aggregate "$m.metacool" --level genome -o "$SCRATCH/$ds.genomes.cool"
done
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-aggregate
#| tbl-cap: "Genome-level aggregation: wall-clock seconds, mean ± sd (n runs), warm and cold, and the edges each network has (they must agree)."
#| code-fold: true
def edges(path):
    e = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", header=None, names=["a", "b", "n"], keep_default_na=False)
    e[["a", "b"]] = np.sort(e[["a", "b"]].to_numpy(), axis=1)
    return e.groupby(["a", "b"])["n"].sum()

check = []
for ds in DATASETS:
    nets = {tool: edges(QUERIES / f"{ds}.{tool}.network.tsv").sort_index()
            for tool in ("metacooler", "cooler") if finished("aggregate", ds, tool, "genome network")}
    missing = [tool for tool in ("cooler", "metacooler") if tool not in nets]
    net = next(iter(nets.values()), None)
    check.append({
        "dataset": ds,
        "edges": "–" if net is None else f"{len(net):,}",
        "contacts": "–" if net is None else f"{net.sum():,}",
        "same as cooler": f"{' and '.join(missing)} did not finish" if missing
                          else "yes" if nets["cooler"].equals(nets["metacooler"]) else "NO",
    })
check = pd.DataFrame(check)
assert not (check["same as cooler"] == "NO").any(), "the two networks differ"
both_caches = pd.concat([wide("aggregate").assign(cache="warm"), wide("aggregate", cache="cold").assign(cache="cold")])
display(show(both_caches[["tool", "task", "cache", *[d for d in DATASETS if d in both_caches.columns]]]))
display(show(wide("aggregate", "peak_mb", digits=0).rename(columns={"task": "task (peak MB)"})))
show(check)
```

## Summary

```{python}
#| label: fig-commands
#| fig-cap: "Every command on the four simulated datasets (simulate.py; no real data), cooler in orange, metacooler in blue. A–F, wall clock against the number of contigs: a line joins the means of a command's runs, each run is a dot and the bar spans them. In C–F, solid lines are warm runs (inputs in the page cache) and dashed lines with open markers cold ones (inputs evicted before every run). A run stopped by timeout at the time limit (dotted line) is a bar with an arrow up, drawn where it was killed: a measured lower bound, which no line joins and nothing extrapolates; the runs that did not finish are named below the figure. G, peak memory of map creation against the number of contigs; H, peak memory of every command on the largest dataset (warm runs; an arrow marks the memory a stopped run held when stopped). Dashed in G and H, the RAM of the machine the runs were on. I, size on disk of the map with its genomes: one .metacool, the .cool with its binning tables or alone, or one .cool per MAG (section 2, which also gives what each holds)."
#| code-fold: true
t = timings()
RAM = ram(t)
PANELS = [
    ("create", ["cload pairs", "create pairs"], "create a map"),
    ("zoomify", ["zoomify"], "zoomify"),
    ("query", ["contig"], "dump a contig"),
    ("query", ["genome"], "dump a genome"),
    ("query", ["genome pair"], "dump a genome pair"),
    ("aggregate", ["genome network"], "genome network"),
]
STORE_STYLE = {
    ".metacool": dict(color=HUE["metacooler"], marker="o"),
    ".cool + binning tables": dict(color=HUE["cooler"], marker="o"),
    ".cool alone (no genomes)": dict(color=HUE["cooler"], marker="o", ls=(0, (1, 1.5)), mfc=SURFACE),
    "one .cool per MAG": dict(color=HUE["cooler"], marker="D", ls=(0, (6, 2)), ms=4),
}


def memory_at(ax, ds):
    """Peak memory of every command on one dataset, cooler and metacooler on one row."""
    rows = runs(t, dataset=ds, cache="warm")
    top = 0.0
    for i, (section, tasks, title) in enumerate(PANELS):
        y = len(PANELS) - 1 - i
        at = {}
        for tool in ("cooler", "metacooler"):
            r = rows[(rows["section"] == section) & rows["task"].isin(tasks) & (rows["tool"] == tool)]
            if not len(r):
                continue
            ok, last = r[r["status"] == "ok"], r["status"].iloc[-1]
            if len(ok):
                at[tool] = ok["peak_gb"].max()
                ax.scatter([at[tool]], [y], s=40, color=HUE[tool], zorder=3)
            elif last in ("timeout", "oom") and r["peak_gb"].notna().any():
                at[tool] = r["peak_gb"].max()
                ax.scatter([at[tool]], [y], marker="|" if last == "timeout" else "X", s=90,
                           color=HUE[tool], lw=2.5, zorder=3)
                if last == "timeout":
                    ax.annotate("", xy=(at[tool] * 1.25 + 0.3, y), xytext=(at[tool], y), zorder=3,
                                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=HUE[tool], lw=1.5, mutation_scale=9))
            elif last == "skipped":
                ax.annotate(f"{tool} not run", (0.02, y), xycoords=("axes fraction", "data"),
                            xytext=(0, -9), textcoords="offset points", color=INK2, fontsize=7.5)
        if len(at) == 2:
            ax.plot(list(at.values()), [y, y], color=GRID, lw=4, zorder=1, solid_capstyle="round")
        top = max([top, *at.values()])
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(PANELS)), [title for _, _, title in reversed(PANELS)])
    ax.set_ylim(-0.7, len(PANELS) - 0.3)
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ram_line(ax, RAM, vertical=True)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(top, RAM if RAM == RAM else 0) * 1.12)
    ax.set_xlabel(f"peak memory on {ds} (GB)")


fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(10.5, 10.4), layout="constrained")
axes = axes.ravel()
for ax, letter, (section, tasks, title) in zip(axes, "ABCDEF", PANELS):
    rows = t[(t["section"] == section) & t["task"].isin(tasks)]
    scaling(ax, rows)
    seconds_axis(ax)
    limit_line(ax, rows)
    ax.set_title(f"{letter}   {title}")
    if ax not in (axes[0], axes[3]):
        ax.set_ylabel("")
    if ax in axes[:3]:
        ax.set_xlabel("")
axes[0].legend(handles=TOOLS_LEGEND, loc="lower right")
axes[2].legend(handles=CACHE_LEGEND, loc="upper left")

g = axes[6]
create = runs(t, section="create")
scaling(g, create, "peak_gb")
log_y(g, "peak memory (GB)")
ram_line(g, RAM)
g.set_title("G   memory: create a map")

memory_at(axes[7], DATASETS[-1])
axes[7].set_title(f"H   memory: every command, {DATASETS[-1]}")

i = axes[8]
for option, r in STORAGE[STORAGE["option"].isin(list(STORE_STYLE))].groupby("option", sort=False):
    i.plot(r["contigs"], r["mb"], label=option, **{"ms": 5, **STORE_STYLE[option]})
contig_axis(i)
log_y(i, "size on disk (MB)")
i.set_title("I   size on disk")
i.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7.5)
save(fig, "commands")
```

```{python}
ENDED = t[t["status"].isin(["timeout", "oom"])]
said = []
for r in ENDED.itertuples():
    what = (f"was **stopped by `timeout` at the {human(TIMEOUT)} time limit**, after {human(r.wall_s)}"
            if r.status == "timeout" else f"was **killed by the kernel for want of memory** after {human(r.wall_s)}")
    held = f", holding {r.peak_gb:.1f} GB" if r.peak_gb == r.peak_gb else ""
    said.append(f"`{command(r.section, r.tool, r.task)}` on {r.dataset} ({CONTIGS[r.dataset]:,} contigs, {r.cache}) "
                f"{what}{held}")
if said:
    print("**Runs that did not finish.** " + "; ".join(said) + ". Each was really run until then: its time and "
          "memory are measured where it ended, lower bounds, not extrapolations, and no line joins them to the "
          "runs that finished. A command that did not finish is not run again."
          + (" A pipeline stopped this way has no peak memory: its shell is killed before it reaps its stages,"
             " whose memory then never reaches GNU time." if ENDED["peak_mb"].isna().any() else ""))
else:
    print(f"Every run finished within the {human(TIMEOUT)} time limit.")
```

How many times faster metacooler runs than cooler (wall clock, means over runs); `>` where
cooler was stopped at the time limit, which makes the ratio a lower bound. cooler's pyramid is
not run where it could not build the base map.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-folds
#| tbl-cap: "Speed-up: cooler's wall clock over metacooler's, warm and cold."
#| code-fold: true
FOLDS = [
    ("create", "cload pairs", "create pairs", "create a map from pairs", "warm"),
    ("zoomify", "zoomify", "zoomify", "zoomify", "warm"),
    ("query", "contig", "contig", "dump a contig", "warm"),
    ("query", "contig", "contig", "dump a contig", "cold"),
    ("query", "genome", "genome", "dump a genome", "warm"),
    ("query", "genome", "genome", "dump a genome", "cold"),
    ("query", "genome pair", "genome pair", "dump a genome pair", "warm"),
    ("query", "genome pair", "genome pair", "dump a genome pair", "cold"),
    ("aggregate", "genome network", "genome network", "genome network", "warm"),
    ("aggregate", "genome network", "genome network", "genome network", "cold"),
]


def fold(section, cooler_task, metacooler_task, ds, cache="warm"):
    """cooler's seconds over metacooler's, and how cooler's run ended: "ok",
    "timeout" (the ratio is then a lower bound), "oom" or "skipped" (no ratio)."""
    pick = runs(t, section=section, dataset=ds, cache=cache)
    c = pick[(pick["tool"] == "cooler") & (pick["task"] == cooler_task)]
    m = pick[(pick["tool"] == "metacooler") & (pick["task"] == metacooler_task) & (pick["status"] == "ok")]
    if c.empty or m.empty:
        return None
    if (c["status"] == "ok").any():
        return c.loc[c["status"] == "ok", "wall_s"].mean() / m["wall_s"].mean(), "ok"
    if (c["status"] == "timeout").any():
        return c["wall_s"].max() / m["wall_s"].mean(), "timeout"
    for status in ("oom", "skipped"):
        if (c["status"] == status).any():
            return None, status
    return None


def fold_text(f):
    match f:
        case None:
            return ""
        case value, "ok":
            return f"{value:,.1f}×"
        case value, "timeout":
            return f"> {value:,.1f}×"
        case _, "skipped":
            return "cooler not run"
        case _:
            return "cooler out of memory"


rows = []
for section, ct, mt, label, cache in FOLDS:
    row = {"": label, "cache": cache}
    for ds in DATASETS:
        row[ds] = fold_text(fold(section, ct, mt, ds, cache))
    rows.append(row)
FOLD_TABLE = pd.DataFrame(rows)
FOLD_TABLE.to_csv(RESULTS / "speedups.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
show(FOLD_TABLE)
```

### Replicates

How much the runs of a command vary: the number of runs *n* of each command on each dataset,
and their coefficient of variation (sd / mean). A command runs at least 3 times unless a
single run takes longer than the threshold below, or it is stopped at the time limit.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-replicates
#| tbl-cap: "Runs per command, dataset and cache state: n, and the coefficient of variation of their wall clock (sd / mean). One run: its time instead."
#| code-fold: true
ok = t[t["status"] == "ok"]
REPS = (
    ok.groupby(["section", "tool", "task", "cache", "dataset"], sort=False)["wall_s"]
    .agg(n="count", mean="mean", sd="std", fastest="min", slowest="max")
    .reset_index()
)
REPS["cv"] = REPS["sd"] / REPS["mean"]
REPS.to_csv(RESULTS / "replicates.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
REPS["cell"] = [f"n={n} · {cv:.1%}" if n > 1 else f"n=1 · {human(mean)}"
                for n, cv, mean in zip(REPS["n"], REPS["cv"], REPS["mean"])]
grid = REPS.pivot(index=["section", "tool", "task", "cache"], columns="dataset", values="cell")
grid = grid.reindex(list(dict.fromkeys(zip(REPS["section"], REPS["tool"], REPS["task"], REPS["cache"]))))
show(grid.reindex(columns=[d for d in DATASETS if d in grid.columns]).reset_index())
```

```{python}
#| label: replicates-summary
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
three = REPS[REPS["n"] >= 3]
once = REPS[REPS["n"] == 1]
worst = three.loc[three["cv"].idxmax()] if len(three) else None
said = [
    f"{len(three)} of {len(REPS)} command × dataset × cache combinations ran at least 3 times"
    + (f"; across them the coefficient of variation has a median of **{three['cv'].median():.1%}**"
       f" and a maximum of **{worst['cv']:.1%}** (`{command(worst['section'], worst['tool'], worst['task'])}`,"
       f" {worst['cache']}, {worst['dataset']})." if worst is not None else ".")
]
if len(once):
    said.append(
        f"{len(once)} ran once{f', each for over {human(LONG)}' if (once['mean'] > LONG).all() else ''}: "
        + "; ".join(f"`{command(r.section, r.tool, r.task)}` ({r.cache}) on {r.dataset}, {human(r.mean)}"
                    for r in once.itertuples())
        + "."
    )
if len(ENDED):
    said.append(f"{len(ENDED)} did not finish and were not repeated (named under the summary figure).")
print(" ".join(said))
```

### Numbers for the text

Filled in from this render; the sentences follow the manuscript draft.

```{python}
#| label: manuscript
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
def mean_wall(section, ds, tool, task, cache="warm"):
    """Mean wall clock of the runs that finished, and how the command ended."""
    r = runs(t, section=section, dataset=ds, tool=tool, task=task, cache=cache)
    ok = r[r.status == "ok"]["wall_s"]
    if len(ok):
        return ok.mean(), "ok"
    for status in ("timeout", "oom"):
        if (r.status == status).any():
            return r.loc[r.status == status, "wall_s"].max(), status
    return None, None


def peak(section, ds, tool, task):
    """The largest peak memory of a command's warm runs (GB)."""
    r = runs(t, section=section, dataset=ds, tool=tool, task=task, cache="warm")
    return r["peak_mb"].max() / 1024


def times(f):
    """A fold as the text says it: 5.6-fold, 41-fold."""
    return f"{f:.1f}" if f < 10 else f"{f:.0f}"


def series(values):
    """'a at 1,000, b at 20,000 and c at 200,000 contigs', from {dataset: text}."""
    parts = [f"**{v}** at {CONTIGS[ds]:,}" for ds, v in values.items()]
    if not parts:
        return "–"
    return (", ".join(parts[:-1]) + " and " if len(parts) > 1 else "") + parts[-1] + " contigs"


def walls(section, tool, task, cache="warm"):
    out = {}
    for ds in DATASETS:
        s, ended = mean_wall(section, ds, tool, task, cache)
        if s is not None:
            out[ds] = {"timeout": "> ", "oom": "out of memory after "}.get(ended, "") + human(s)
    return out


cooler_v, mc_v = version("cooler"), version("metacooler")
last = DATASETS[-1]
lines = [
    f"* All benchmarks are on simulated data: {['one', 'two', 'three', 'four'][len(DATASETS) - 1] if len(DATASETS) <= 4 else len(DATASETS)} "
    f"communities drawn by `simulate.py` (generator "
    f"v{SUMMARY[last]['generator_version']}) from a fixed seed each, of {CONTIGS[DATASETS[0]]:,} to "
    f"{CONTIGS[last]:,} contigs. No real reads, assembly or binning is used, and there are no accessions."
]
cooler_built = [ds for ds in DATASETS if mean_wall("create", ds, "cooler", "cload pairs")[1] == "ok"]
if cooler_built:
    ds = cooler_built[-1]
    f, _ = fold("create", "cload pairs", "create pairs", ds)
    lines.append(
        f"* metacooler {mc_v} creates metacool files **{times(f)}-fold** faster than cooler v{cooler_v} "
        f"creates the equivalent .cool file for an assembly of **{CONTIGS[ds]:,} contigs** "
        f"({human(mean_wall('create', ds, 'metacooler', 'create pairs')[0])} against "
        f"{human(mean_wall('create', ds, 'cooler', 'cload pairs')[0])}), while also ingesting and indexing "
        f"the /genomes table."
    )
for ds in DATASETS:
    c, ended = mean_wall("create", ds, "cooler", "cload pairs")
    m, _ = mean_wall("create", ds, "metacooler", "create pairs")
    if ended == "timeout":
        why = (f"was stopped by `timeout` at the {human(TIMEOUT)} time limit, holding "
               f"{peak('create', ds, 'cooler', 'cload pairs'):.1f} GB: {human(c)} is where it was killed, "
               f"a measured lower bound, not an extrapolation")
    elif ended == "oom":
        why = f"ran out of memory ({RAM:.0f} GB) after {human(c)}"
    else:
        continue
    lines.append(
        f"* At **{CONTIGS[ds]:,} contigs** ({SUMMARY[ds]['genomes']:,} genomes), `cooler cload pairs` {why}; "
        f"metacooler took {human(m)} (peak {peak('create', ds, 'metacooler', 'create pairs'):.1f} GB)."
    )
peaks = runs(t, dataset=last, cache="warm")
peaks = peaks[peaks["status"] == "ok"]
if len(peaks):
    top = {tool: r.loc[r["peak_mb"].idxmax()] for tool, r in peaks.groupby("tool")}
    said = [f"`{command(r['section'], tool, r['task'])}`, {r['peak_mb'] / 1024:.1f} GB" for tool, r in top.items()]
    lines.append(
        f"* Every command ran on one machine with **{RAM:.1f} GB** of RAM ({int(t['cores'].iloc[0])} cores). "
        f"On {CONTIGS[last]:,} contigs, the largest peak of each tool, among the runs that finished: "
        + " and ".join(said) + "."
    )
store = STORAGE[STORAGE["dataset"] == last].set_index("option")
if len(store):
    mags = store.loc["one .cool per MAG"]
    lines.append(
        f"* On disk, at {CONTIGS[last]:,} contigs: **{store.loc['.metacool', 'mb']:,.0f} MB** for the .metacool, "
        f"{store.loc['.cool + binning tables', 'mb']:,.0f} MB for the .cool and its binning tables "
        f"({store.loc['.cool alone (no genomes)', 'mb']:,.0f} MB for the .cool alone), and "
        f"{mags['mb']:,.0f} MB for {mags['files']:,} per-MAG .cool files, which hold only "
        f"{MAG_SHARE[last]['contacts']:.0%} of the contacts and {MAG_SHARE[last]['contigs']:.0%} of the contigs."
    )
if walls("query", "cooler", "genome"):
    share = SHARE.get((last, "genome"))
    warm_fold, cold_fold = fold("query", "genome", "genome", last), fold("query", "genome", "genome", last, "cold")
    lines.append(
        "* With cooler's command line, extracting a single MAG from a genome-agnostic .cool file is a "
        "linear scan of every pixel (`cooler dump --join`, filtered against the binning table): "
        f"{series(walls('query', 'cooler', 'genome'))} (warm). `metacooler dump -r <MAG>` takes "
        f"{series(walls('query', 'metacooler', 'genome'))} warm, and "
        f"{series(walls('query', 'metacooler', 'genome', 'cold'))} cold."
        + (f" On the simulated {CONTIGS[last]:,}-contig map that is {fold_text(warm_fold)} warm and "
           f"{fold_text(cold_fold)} cold. cooler's scan reads every pixel of the map, metacooler only the "
           f"MAG's ({share:.2%} of them here), so the fold depends on how a map's pixels split between its "
           f"genomes: here the simulated community sets that, not a real sample." if warm_fold and share else "")
    )
agg, _ = mean_wall("aggregate", last, "metacooler", "genome-level .cool")
if agg is not None:
    s = SUMMARY[last]
    net, _ = mean_wall("aggregate", last, "metacooler", "genome network")
    scan, scan_ended = mean_wall("aggregate", last, "cooler", "genome network")
    lines.append(
        f"* A full genome-by-genome aggregated matrix is computed in **{human(agg)}** for a simulated community of "
        f"**{s['genomes']:,} genomes** ({s['mags']:,} MAGs and {s['mge_bins']:,} small bins; "
        f"{CONTIGS[last]:,} contigs, {s['pairs'] / 1e6:,.0f} M read pairs; "
        f"`metacooler aggregate --level genome`). Its edge list takes {human(net)} "
        f"(`metacooler network --level genome`), against "
        f"{'> ' if scan_ended == 'timeout' else ''}{human(scan)} for cooler's scan."
    )
if len(three):
    lo, hi = int(three["n"].min()), int(REPS["n"].max())
    lines.append(
        f"* Timings are means over {lo if lo == hi else f'{lo}–{hi}'} runs"
        + (f" (one, for a run over {human(LONG)})" if (once["mean"] > LONG).any() else "")
        + f"; their coefficient of variation has a median of {three['cv'].median():.1%}."
    )
print("\n".join(lines))
```

```{python}
#| label: artifacts

def link(path):
    """A file's name, linked when the page can reach it: written beside the page (the
    notebook's directory), as _results/ is unless BENCH_RESULTS moves it."""
    name, href = str(path.relative_to(RESULTS)), os.path.relpath(path)
    return name if href.startswith("..") else f'<a href="{href}">{name}</a>'


files = sorted(p for p in RESULTS.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
show(pd.DataFrame({
    "file": [link(p) for p in files],
    "kB": [p.stat().st_size / 1e3 for p in files],
}), **{"kB": "{:,.1f}"})
```

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `timings.tsv` | every timed run: command, cache state, status, wall/CPU seconds, peak memory, output size, versions, machine |
| `datasets.tsv` | the datasets table above |
| `storage.tsv` | the size on disk of each way to keep the map, per dataset |
| `speedups.tsv` | the fold table above |
| `replicates.tsv` | per command, dataset and cache state: runs, mean, sd, fastest, slowest, coefficient of variation |
| `figures/` | every figure, PNG and SVG |
